ogTitle: Bangkok Shopping Plan: 3 Days — Siam, Ratchaprasong, Chatuchak & Markets
ogDesc: Shop Bangkok smart in 3 days: malls around Siam–Ratchaprasong, the Chatuchak Weekend Market, then a night market — with real opening hours.
intro: Bangkok is hard to beat as a shopping city. You get luxury malls running for a kilometre straight under the skytrain, the biggest weekend market in the world, and night markets where you can eat and shop until 1am. The only problem is there's so much you don't know where to start. So we've split it into 3 days that flow nicely on foot: day one walks all the malls around Siam–Ratchaprasong in one go by BTS, day two takes on Chatuchak and Or Tor Kor from the morning, and day three rounds it off at a night market — with real opening hours and honest ballpark prices throughout.

blocks.html: What makes Bangkok shopping special is that you can shop on any budget in one city. Want to browse designer brands in cold air-con? The Siam–Ratchaprasong area has malls lined up one after another under the skywalk. Want to haggle and hunt for something unusual? There's Chatuchak and the night markets. This plan is laid out so you can just follow it day by day, with no backtracking — each day stays in one zone to save travel time.

blocks.title: Read this before you head out
blocks.html: Chatuchak is busiest only on the weekend (Sat–Sun), while the night markets run from evening until late. If you can line up your Chatuchak day with the weekend and keep your mall-walking day for a weekday, you'll find the fullest selection and fewer crowds.

blocks.text: Day 1 — Mall-hopping around Siam–Ratchaprasong all day

blocks.html: Today you barely need to take any transport, because the malls around Siam and Ratchaprasong are linked by a continuous skywalk under the BTS. You can walk from National Stadium all the way to Chit Lom without ever stepping down to street level. Start with the cheaper malls first, then work your way up to the luxury ones in the afternoon.

blocks.label: Day 1
blocks.title: Siam → Ratchaprasong (mall to mall on foot)

items.note: Get off at BTS National Stadium — there's a walkway straight into the mall. It's an old-school budget mall: clothes, bags, phone cases. The 4th floor is all phones, SIM cards and IT gear, and you can haggle. Open 10:00–22:00.

items.activity: Cross over to Siam Discovery + Siam Center
items.note: Everything is connected by walkways. Siam Discovery leans into design, homeware and new Thai brands; Siam Center is all Thai designer fashion. Both are great to wander and photograph.

items.activity: Lunch break at Siam Paragon, ground floor (Gourmet Market / food court)
items.note: Paragon is open 10:00–22:00. The basement has a super-premium supermarket and tons of restaurants — a good spot to refuel before walking on.
Across from Paragon, this is the outdoor zone: youth-oriented shops, cafés, indie Thai brands at friendly prices. Great for strolling and photos.

items.activity: Head to CentralWorld via the skywalk
items.note: A huge mall with over 600 shops across 7 floors — fashion, homeware and restaurants. Open 10:00–22:00. The plaza out front is an event space that often has something going on.

Right next to CentralWorld on the Ratchaprasong intersection side, these are high-end designer malls. Even if you don't buy, they're worth a look for the design. Nearby is the Erawan Shrine if you want to stop and pay respects.

items.activity: Finish with quick shopping at Platinum Fashion Mall in Pratunam
items.note: Walk from Chit Lom along the skywalk toward Pratunam, or take a short motorbike taxi. This is a wholesale clothing mall with 2,500+ shops — cheap if you buy several pieces. Closes around 20:00 (some zones close earlier, so check first).

blocks.title: Tip for the mall day
blocks.html: A single-trip BTS ticket is enough, since today you're mostly on the skywalk and barely ride the train. Comfortable shoes matter a lot — you'll walk several kilometres in total. Every mall is freezing with air-con, so it's worth carrying a light layer.

blocks.text: What each Siam–Ratchaprasong mall is known for

items.name: Siam Paragon
items.blurb: Upscale mall in the centre of Siam, with high-end brands, a premium supermarket and plenty of restaurants. Open 10:00–22:00.

items.name: CentralWorld
items.blurb: The biggest mall in the Ratchaprasong area, with over 600 shops covering fashion, lifestyle and food. Open 10:00–22:00.

items.name: MBK Center
items.blurb: The legendary budget mall: clothes, bags, phones, SIM cards and IT gear, and you can haggle. Open 10:00–22:00.

items.name: Platinum Fashion Mall
items.blurb: A wholesale clothing market in Pratunam with 2,500+ shops — the more you buy, the cheaper it gets. Good for buyers who plan to resell.

blocks.text: Day 2 — Chatuchak + Or Tor Kor Market from the morning

blocks.html: Chatuchak is the biggest weekend market in the world, split into 27 sections by product category — from clothes, homeware, plants and pets to crafts and vintage. It gets crowded and hot, so the trick is to arrive before 10am while it's still less packed, then cross over for a break and good food at Or Tor Kor across the road.

items.activity: Arrive at Chatuchak in the morning
items.note: Get off at MRT Kamphaeng Phet (you come straight up into the market), or BTS Mo Chit / MRT Chatuchak Park. Open Sat–Sun 9:00–18:00, plus a Friday wholesale round 18:00–24:00. Arrive early for the fullest selection, fewer people and weaker sun.
Handmade clothes, indie Thai brands, bags and shoes, with prices starting in the low hundreds of baht. You can haggle, especially if you buy several pieces.
Woodwork, ceramics and well-designed homeware, much cheaper than in the malls. A favourite spot for people decorating homes and cafés.

items.activity: Cross over for lunch at Or Tor Kor Market
items.note: Opposite MRT Kamphaeng Phet, open daily 6:00–20:00. It's a premium fresh market with gorgeous fruit and delicious ready-to-eat food, and it's air-conditioned — a great spot to escape the heat.

items.activity: Go back for the plant + vintage zones (Sections 2–4, plant side)
items.note: The plant and garden zone is lively, and there's vintage stuff, vinyl records, collectibles and antiques. Fun to walk even if you don't buy.

items.activity: Café break inside Chatuchak before heading back
items.note: Cafés are scattered throughout the market — a place to sit out of the heat and rehydrate before the trip back in the evening.

blocks.title: Surviving Chatuchak
blocks.html: Bring plenty of cash and water — many small stalls still only take cash, and it gets very hot in the afternoon. If you get lost, note the Section and lane numbers (written on the posts), and agree on a meeting point in case you get separated.

blocks.text: Day 3 — Night market, eat and shop as you go

blocks.html: Save your energy for the evening on the last day, because Bangkok's night markets only get going after 5pm and run late. The appeal is eating and shopping in one place — food, fashion, vintage finds, and pretty lit-up scenes that are fun to photograph. Pick one based on where you're staying.

items.note: Right by MRT Rama 9 Exit 1 (next to Big C), open daily 17:00–01:00. The food is a big draw — famous for spicy pork-bone soup (leng saep) and desserts — plus secondhand fashion and a young crowd. The easiest one to reach.
Rows of street-food stalls, savoury and sweet, with seating in the middle of the market and friendly prices.

Open Thu–Sun 17:00–01:00. It's farther out (near Seacon Square, you'll need a taxi) but stands out for vintage goods, collectibles, classic cars and antique warehouses — great for homeware and antique hunters in particular.
Night markets are a good-value place for souvenirs — Thai-print tees, keychains, snacks and gifts. You can haggle if you buy several.

blocks.title: 2026 update
blocks.html: The original JODD Fairs Rama 9 closed back in early 2025 and has since merged into the Ratchada branch (next to MRT Rama 9). JJ Green, the vintage market next to Chatuchak, has also closed permanently. If you're after vintage, head to Train Night Market Srinakarin instead.

blocks.text: What each area is best for — pick by your style

items.name: Siam (Siam Paragon / Discovery / Center / Square)
items.blurb: The hub of fashion and lifestyle, with a continuous run of air-conditioned malls covering both new Thai labels and big international brands. Right by BTS Siam, the interchange of the skytrain lines.

items.name: Ratchaprasong (CentralWorld / Gaysorn / Erawan)
items.blurb: The biggest cluster of upscale malls, connected straight on from Siam by skywalk. Ranges from a huge do-everything mall to high-end designer ones. Close to the Erawan Shrine.

items.name: Chatuchak (Weekend Market)
items.blurb: The biggest weekend market in the world, 27 sections packed with everything from clothes, homeware, plants and pets to vintage. You can haggle. Come early to dodge the heat and crowds.

items.name: Pratunam (Platinum Fashion Mall + Pratunam Market)
items.blurb: The capital of wholesale clothing — the more you buy, the cheaper it gets. Good for resellers or buying in sets, and you can walk on from Ratchaprasong.
items.meta: BTS Chit Lom + walk/motorbike taxi · Closes around 20:00

items.name: Or Tor Kor Market
items.blurb: A premium fresh market opposite Chatuchak with gorgeous fruit, great food and ready-to-eat dishes, all air-conditioned. A solid place to break for a meal while walking Chatuchak.

items.name: JODD Fairs Ratchada (night market)
items.blurb: A popular night market where you eat and shop as you go — strong on food, secondhand fashion and a young crowd. Right by MRT Rama 9, the easiest to reach.

items.name: Train Night Market Srinakarin (vintage)
items.blurb: A vintage-focused night market with antiques, classic cars and collectible warehouses, plus pretty neon-lit scenes for photos. It's far out and needs a taxi — best for homeware and antique lovers.

blocks.text: Roughly how much will this trip cost

items: BTS/MRT transport — around ฿60–120 a day depending on how many trips; a Rabbit/MRT stored-value card is more convenient.
Food — mall food courts run ฿60–150 a plate, market stalls ฿40–120 a plate, roughly ฿300–600 per person per day.
Shopping budget — flexible, up to you. Budget finds at MBK/Chatuchak/Pratunam start in the low hundreds, while brand-name goods in Siam–Ratchaprasong are at full price.
End-of-trip souvenirs — night markets are the best-value place for gifts; tees, keychains and snacks start in the low tens of baht.

blocks.title: How to haggle
blocks.html: In markets and wholesale malls, haggling is normal. Try asking for a discount when you buy several pieces — being polite and smiling usually gets you a better price. But the upscale malls in Siam–Ratchaprasong have fixed prices, so there's no bargaining there.

faq.q: Which days is Chatuchak Weekend Market open?
faq.a: It's busiest on Saturday and Sunday, open 9:00–18:00. Friday is the evening wholesale round, 18:00–24:00, and there's also a plant-market zone open Wednesday–Thursday. If you're visiting, plan your Chatuchak day for a Saturday or Sunday for the fullest selection.

faq.q: Which train line do I use to walk Siam–Ratchaprasong?
faq.a: Mainly the BTS Sukhumvit Line. Get off at Siam for Siam Paragon/Center/Discovery and Siam Square, National Stadium for MBK, and Chit Lom for CentralWorld/Gaysorn. They're all connected by skywalk, so you barely need to step down to the street.

faq.q: Are JODD Fairs Rama 9 and JJ Green still open?
faq.a: The original JODD Fairs Rama 9 branch closed back in early 2025 and has merged into the Ratchada branch (by MRT Rama 9, next to Big C), open daily 17:00–01:00. JJ Green, the vintage market next to Chatuchak, has closed permanently — for vintage, we'd suggest Train Night Market Srinakarin instead.

faq.q: Where's the best place to find cheap goods in Bangkok?
faq.a: Good-value wholesale clothing at Platinum Fashion Mall in Pratunam, odds and ends and phones at MBK, and handmade goods, homeware and vintage at friendly prices in Chatuchak. You can haggle everywhere — the more you buy, the cheaper it gets.

faq.q: Chatuchak is so hot — is there anywhere to escape the heat?
faq.a: Yes. Cross over to Or Tor Kor Market opposite MRT Kamphaeng Phet, an indoor air-conditioned market with great food and lovely fruit, or stop at one of the cafés scattered throughout Chatuchak. We'd suggest carrying water and coming in the morning before the sun gets strong.
